claim_ceiling: The exact Codex CLI binary completed one owner-assisted registered synthetic-workspace mem_current_project call after the CLI selected that workspace with -C. The returned cwd matched the selected workspace, the source-bound wrapper used process cwd, and the same registry resolved that cwd through its approved Git remote. This is one positive CLI signal case, not a supported adapter or evidence for Codex Desktop.
limitations: The execution timestamp is derived from the first retained synthetic Engram database artifact timestamp rather than a host-issued tool-call timestamp.

The wrapper was observed with the expected environment-key absences, but its transient process exited before the operating-system cwd probe returned a path. Workspace provenance therefore combines the Codex workdir, the provider-returned cwd, the exact wrapper source and hash, and pre-run resolver proof.
The PATH-alias warning concerned refused helper creation under the disposable temporary Codex home; the exact absolute CLI executable still ran and completed the MCP call.

Codex populated built-in skills, caches, local state databases, and a remote plugin catalogue inside the fresh disposable Codex home. No existing user credentials, settings, plugins, hooks, or production Codex configuration were copied.
Credential key names were absent at the observed wrapper process, but no explicit credential canaries were injected; the complete credential-isolation case remains unrun.

Unregistered, missing-remote, inherited-project refusal, registry-collision, provider-unavailable, nested, linked-worktree, same-basename, sequential or concurrent multi-project, restart, instruction-lifecycle, Desktop, and other-platform cases remain unrun.
No memory content was read or saved; memory read and write correctness were not tested.
The clean-quit probes are point-in-time evidence and do not establish crash, force-quit, or universal lifecycle behavior.
